paragraphs: R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak (1). (A Tanna of baraitot). In Sukkah 11b they said: '[Shall we say it is] like [a dispute of] Tannaim' — the words of R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak; and he was the teacher of R' Yochanan, as in Yoma 43b, where they said: it is not only a Tanna whom he did not heed, but even his own teacher (R' Sh[imon] ben Yehotzadak) he likewise did not heed. And in Rosh Hashanah 34b they said of him: it is not difficult — this is his own [view], that is his teacher's (R' Sh[imon] ben Yehotzadak).

And likewise R' Yochanan said [teachings] in the name of R' Sh[imon] ben Yehotzadak, as in Pesachim 95 [supplied 'צה;']; Sukkah 27 [supplied 'כז,']; Taanit 28 [supplied 'כח;']; Yevamot 79 [supplied 'עט;']; Ketubot 72 [supplied 'עב;']; Bava Batra 96 [supplied 'צו,']; Sanhedrin 74b, 90 [supplied 'צ;']; Avodah Zarah 47 [supplied 'מז,']; Niddah 6 [supplied 'ו;']; Maasrot ch. 3 hal. 1; Orlah beginning of ch. 1; Pesachim ch. 2 end of hal. 2. Hyman identifies him as a kohen and reports that he died in Lod, as in Semachot ch. 4 hal. 11, where they said: it happened that Shimon ben

Yehotzadak died in Lod, and Yochanan his brother came from the Galilee to become impure for him. Hyman adds that R' Yochanan was present at his death, as in Yerushalmi Nazir ch. 7 hal. 1 and Kohelet Rabbah ch. 7 at the supplied verse locator ביה, where R' Yochanan asked R' Yannai before the bier of R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak; and the statement is cited in Berakhot ch. 3 end of hal. 1, and Hyman says that there it erroneously reads 'R' Shmuel b. Y.'. And what they said in Pesachim ch. 2 at the beginning of hal. 3, R' Shimon

ben Elazar in the name of R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak—Hyman considers this a scribal error and says it should read 'in the name of R' Shimon ben Yochai'; it crept in there from the preceding line, where it is written: R' Yochanan said in the name of R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak. Hyman concludes: And this is clear.

notes.text: The earlier teacher and the later namesake in entry45 remain distinct in Hyman’s account. Yochanan the brother who became impure and Rabbi Yochanan who asked Yannai are not collapsed.
The Kohelet verse locator ביה remains unresolved. The Shmuel b.Y. reading, Hyman’s Shimon ben Yochai correction and adjacent-line contamination explanation remain his reported variants and argument.

The fresh William Davidson Sukkah11b paragraph names Rabbi Shimon bar Yehotzadak, while the Yoma43b paragraph has Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak and explicitly says that Rabbi Yochanan did not heed even his own teacher. Hyman’s ben form and the two digital forms remain distinct without an authority merge. The heading’s full Rabbi title has local support; the body deliberately retains Hyman’s abbreviated titles as R' rather than transferring a fuller title between passages. Untitled Yochanan the brother and the reporting R' Yochanan remain separate roles. Hyman’s scribal-error claim, should-read correction, preceding-line explanation and emphatic And this is clear remain his argument at full strength, without fresh proof of correction history. The supplied ביה locator and Shmuel b.Y. reading remain unresolved, and L0017-L0024 remains held. Supplied folio marks and first/beginning/end markers are preserved; labels in the new English say supplied rather than claiming printed-pixel verification. Both existing mixed notes and all historical notes remain verbatim. No additional legal teaching or figures from the two digital paragraphs are imported; no historical identity, teacher, priesthood or death-date admission is made.

The whole consulted Sukkah 11b paragraph has Shimon bar Yehotzadak, while Yoma 43b and Rosh Hashanah 34b have ben and explicitly distinguish Rabbi Yochanan’s own view from his teacher’s. The forms and the two roles called Yochanan are not merged. The whole Semachot 4:11 account says that the brother arrived from Galilee after the grave had been closed; the sages forbade his becoming impure and allowed the grave to be opened for him to see. Hyman’s shorter account is retained. The whole consulted Yerushalmi Nazir 7:1 and Berakhot 3:1 passages name Shimon ben Yotzadak at the bier; the Berakhot English apparatus reports a Rome-manuscript Shimon reading against a Leiden Shmuel reading. That is the consulted editor’s report, not a new collation of the manuscript images. The whole Kohelet Rabbah 7:2 passage under “and the living will take it to heart” also has the bier discussion, beside Hyman’s retained literal locator ביה. Yerushalmi Pesachim 2:3 still has Shimon ben Elazar reporting Shimon ben Yotzadak, and the preceding 2:2 contains a Yochanan report in Yotzadak’s name. This permits the textual comparison; Hyman’s proposed Yochai correction, adjacent-line copying explanation and emphatic “this is clear” remain his argument, rather than an adopted emendation or proof of copying history. Other references in the long supplied list have not thereby all been independently verified.
